Welcome to Blue Skies School
Teaching how your child learns
We believe it is important for students to achieve their full potential and to ensure this we offer a rich and stimulating curriculum, individually tailored to our students needs. We reflect good practice in an environment that supports our students learning.
Welcome from the Headteacher
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Blue Skies School, a specialist setting dedicated to providing high-quality, individualised education for high-functioning autistic students. At Blue Skies, we believe that every child has the potential to thrive, and it is our mission to unlock that potential through a supportive, nurturing, and aspirational learning environment.
Our school is built on inclusion, collaboration, and high expectations. We offer a tailored curriculum that blends academic excellence with essential social, emotional, and life skills, ensuring that our students are fully prepared for the next stage of their journey—whether that be further education, employment, or independent living.
At the heart of our approach is a deep understanding of neurodiversity, ensuring that every pupil receives the personalised support they need to flourish. We pride ourselves on working in close partnership with families, carers, and professionals, fostering a sense of belonging and community that extends beyond the classroom. Our dedicated team of educators and support staff is passionate about maximising every pupil’s strengths, helping them to develop confidence, resilience, and independence. At Blue Skies, we celebrate every achievement, no matter how big or small, because we recognise the incredible effort and growth behind each success.
Whether you are a prospective family, a professional looking to collaborate with us, or a visitor keen to learn more about our school, I encourage you to explore our website and reach out to us. Together, we can ensure that every young person at Blue Skies has the opportunity to soar.
Carrie MyhillHeadteacher, Blue Skies School
Our Vision & Values
Safeguarding
Blue Skies Staff
Blue Skies is a school, based in Medway, which offers a unique service to children and young adults on the autism spectrum.
It is a caring school with a holistic approach towards education, catering for students in Medway, Kent and the surrounding areas.
This website is designed for parents and professionals who want to learn more about the school. It will provide some basic information and background reading before a visit.
In order to appreciate the school, we would recommend visiting us. Please call at any time to make an appointment.
Blue Skies School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people and vulnerable adults and expect all staff, volunteers and other third parties to share this commitment. Safer recruitment practice and pre-employment background checks will be undertaken before any appointment is confirmed.

The Curriculum
The Blue Skies Curriculum has been developed in consultation with the students, parents, staff and proprietors to create a bespoke pathway to meet the needs of our learners on the Autism Spectrum.
The curriculum offer meets our School mission, to equip our students with the necessary skills and qualifications to become happy and confident independent people; giving them the support they need in order to successfully transition to further education or employment.
We have ensured that our Curriculum Intent and Implementation have a quantifiable Impact on learners progress and outcomes.

Advisory Board and School Improvement Consultant
Lee Lucas is the Safeguarding Specialist on the Advisory Board at Blue Skies School. She has had a long-standing professional relationship with the school and has delivered safeguarding training to staff for several years, supporting them to stay compliant with statutory guidance and confident in their ability to keep children safe from harm.
With over 30 years of experience in education, Lee has worked across a range of settings, including local authorities and individual schools. She is currently the Head of Safeguarding, Attendance, Exclusion and Admissions for The Thinking Schools Trust, where she supports 26 schools across the South West, South, and South East of England.
Lee is passionate about amplifying the voice of the child and understanding the impact of lived experience on young people. She thoroughly enjoys her visits to Blue Skies and feels privileged to support the school’s continued development as part of the Advisory Board.
Join our Advisory Board
Andrew is currently a school improvement consultant, serving a range of mainstream and special schools on a regular basis. He has worked with Blue Skies School since Autumn 2022. He also leads inspections of independent schools, in the UK and overseas.
Andrew was previously a Headteacher, National Leader of Education and lead Ofsted inspector in the special education schools sector, including experience in residential settings. He has held three successful headships in all-age special schools for pupils of all abilities with cognitive, sensory, autistic, physical and medical conditions, and associated learning difficulties, and social, emotional and mental health issues. He has also been an executive principal of a mainstream, secondary academy in an inner-city area of deprivation, supporting it in its requirement to improve. He has worked internationally to create provision for children with disabilities in challenging situations.

Admissions to Blue Skies School
We believe it is important for students to achieve their full potential and progress to a future of their choice. To ensure this, we offer a rich and stimulating curriculum, individually tailored to our student’s needs, supported by strong pastoral care, social and emotional support and various therapies.
Student starting points
Blue Skies acknowledges that every learner is different, not only with personal interest, but also retained knowledge and skills. At Blue Skies, following a transition period, students are assessed and assigned to an appropriate peer group with a predicted flight path (expected outcomes by the end of each Key Stage). These are regularly reviewed and include personalised learning targets through Person Centered Annual Reviews (PCARs).
Class sizes are limited to a maximum of 8, with many classes around 5 students with two supporting adults (one teacher and one teaching assistant). Class groupings are not linear (i.e. with peers in the same year group), we place students with pupils with similar interest and dynamic where possible; developing the overall wellbeing of an individual empowers them to thrive socially and academically. Practical tasks are used to see the relevance and application of study to real life situations, developing students’ understanding of the world, being able to understand themselves and how they can become fully functioning citizens; utilising their skills in the future.
Admissions process
All students attending Blue Skies must hold a current Education and Healthcare Plan (EHCP) from their respective local authority. Our cohort consist of Medway and Kent children and young people, with a diagnosis or traits of Autism.
Many of our students have experienced an unsettled period of education within mainstream education, and required a smaller bespoke setting to meet their needs.
If you are considering applying for Blue Skies, please liaise with the Education Authority to send us the current EHCP before arranging a tour with the school.
Following the school screening the paperwork issued by the local authority, an Observation and Assessment Day (O&A) will be organised. This includes time with students in school, both socially and within a variety of lessons throughout the morning. A decision on whether a placement is suitable will be shared with the Local authority following this assessment.
